who: Historian of Native American history at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln; PhD in American history, Arizona State University, 2002.

evidence.says: Nebraska faculty biography identifies Victoria Smith as a history professor with an Arizona State PhD in American history (2002), and lists No One Ever Asked Me and Captive Arizona.
Samuel H. Herley’s 2010 Nebraska history dissertation, The Coming Tide, explicitly names Professor Victoria Smith as supervisor.
LC identifies Victoria Smith through No One Ever Asked Me, Captive Arizona, and an Arizona State PhD awarded in 2002.

notes: Direct student-supervisor evidence and the same doctorate and books connect the supervisor to the candidate’s LC identity.

who: Historian of medieval and early modern Europe at Maryland, previously Arizona State; PhD, University of Michigan, 1988.

evidence.says: Maryland biography gives a Michigan PhD in medieval and early modern European history (1988), Arizona State employment in 1989–2005, and Maryland employment beginning in fall 2005; it lists Wondrous in His Saints.
Maryland’s repository identifies Philip Soergel as advisor of Erin Wessell’s Knowing the World: John Dee and His Contemporary Natural Philosophers, dated 2018.
LC identifies Philip M. Soergel as author of Wondrous in His Saints (1993), also listed by his Maryland biography.

notes: Both institutions and the doctorate match. Wessell’s repository record uses a revised title and 2018 date, versus the AHA entry’s 2019; the advisor is explicit.

who: Historian of modern U.S. social policy, criminal justice and drugs at the University of Florida; PhD in history, Carnegie Mellon, 1994.

Florida’s alumni table lists Erin L. Conlin’s spring 2014 history PhD, Invisible Hands in the Winter Garden, with Joseph F. Spillane as advisor.
LC identifies Joseph F. Spillane through Cocaine and Coxsackie; the latter’s authority citation describes him as a University of Florida history professor.

notes: Student, affiliation, doctorate and publications identify the same Joseph F. Spillane.

who: Historian of Nazi Germany and the Holocaust, Nebraska-Lincoln faculty member in 1993–2008, later Vermont; PhD in history, UNC-Chapel Hill, 1988.

who: Historian of early modern Europe, especially Italy and France, at UCLA; PhD in European history, UCLA, 1967.
